name: pdf
transitions: real->protected (CR0.PE 0->1, far jump to flat 32-bit code 0x08)
GDT has only THREE entries (limit 0x17) so selector 0x80 is far past the end
IDT: vector 8 (#DF) -> df_handler with P=1; vector 13 (#GP) -> the SAME target but with P=0, so only the present bit distinguishes them
delivering it finds IDT[13] not present -> #NP(0x6A = 13*8+2) -- also contributory
contributory during contributory => #DF with error code 0 (qemu: `check_exception old: 0xd new 0xb` then `v=08 e=0000`)
df_handler runs at CPL0 and exits; #DF is an ABORT so it does not IRET

delivery_records.what_the_error_code_decides: the handler grades the PUSHED ERROR CODE, not merely which handler ran. IDT[13] and IDT[8] name the same target, so if the machine had skipped the escalation and just delivered the #NP, control would still reach df_handler -- but with error code 0x6A. IA-32 requires #DF's code to be 0 regardless of what either contributing fault carried.
delivery_records.motivating_measurement: before the fix, an undefined opcode against a sparse IDT looped forever: vec=6, then vec=11 err=0x32, then vec=11 err=0x5A repeating. After it, the same image gives four faults and stops -- the last one vec=11 err=0x42 (8*8+2), proving the #DF delivery was attempted before SHUTDOWN.
delivery_records.success_proof: at the exit (CPL0): ebx=0 (#DF error code), ecx=the trigger's DS-load EIP (the ORIGINAL faulting instruction, not either handler), edx=0x08 (saved CS), esi=1 (df_handler entered exactly once), edi=0 (the not-reached marker after the trigger never ran); then out 0xf4 = qemu status 133

description: REVIEW_aug2 H-04 gate: a fault taken DURING delivery must escalate to #DF, and a fault during #DF delivery must shut the machine down. There was no delivery-depth state at all -- start_fault() could re-vector an IDT-limit failure and S_INT_GATE could re-vector bad gate attributes, but each was a documented 'single re-vector', so a fault while delivering a fault just started another ordinary delivery and the machine could loop forever. The core now tracks dlv_depth plus the CLASS of what is being delivered (contributory / page fault), because IA-32 6.15 Table 6-5 escalates only for contributory-during-contributory and page-fault combinations -- benign faults and software INT n nest normally. This test isolates the escalation from the privilege machinery: no paging, no CPL3, everything at CPL0. It builds a 3-entry GDT so selector 0x80 gives a clean deterministic #GP(0x80), and an IDT where vector 13 and vector 8 name the SAME handler and differ ONLY in the present bit. That is deliberate: control reaches df_handler either way, so the test grades the PUSHED ERROR CODE (0 for a real #DF, 0x6A for a merely-delivered #NP) and the saved EIP, which must point at the original DS load rather than at any handler. QEMU implements the full table (observed: `check_exception old: 0xd new 0xb` then `v=08 e=0000`), so it is graded differentially. The shutdown half is exercised separately by the ppriv image, whose sparse IDT now terminates in four faults instead of looping.
